stem: Which principle should guide routine preoperative testing for an adult having elective surgery?

options.A: Use the same laboratory and diagnostic panel for every client regardless of health status or procedure.
options.B: Order tests even when the result would not affect perioperative planning.
options.C: Use test results instead of obtaining a preoperative history and clinical assessment.
options.D: Select tests according to the client's health, comorbidities, medications, ASA status, and type of surgery when the result could affect care.

rationale: Current NICE guidance does not recommend one universal preoperative test panel. Testing recommendations vary by surgery grade, ASA grade, comorbidities, medicines, and whether a result would influence management. D is correct.
educational_objective: Use individualized clinical indications rather than blanket panels when considering preoperative testing.
source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
source_document_title: Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery (NG45)
source_locator: Recommendations 1.2, 1.5-1.9; recommendations by surgery grade and ASA grade; Overview
source_claim_supported: Routine preoperative testing is selected according to surgery grade, ASA grade, comorbidities, medicines, and clinical indication; many tests should not be offered routinely in low-risk situations.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — preoperative assessment and interpretation of diagnostic testing
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — individualized preoperative testing

source_original.stem: A nurse reviews preoperative laboratory testing ordered for a client before elective surgery, and a family member assumes every client gets the exact same standard panel regardless of their own health background. The purpose of this testing is generally instead to:

options.A: Order the same fixed laboratory panel for every client regardless of procedure or health status
options.B: Delay scheduling by obtaining routine tests even when results cannot influence perioperative care
options.C: Replace the preoperative history and examination with a standardized set of laboratory results
options.D: Select tests according to clinical history, comorbidities, procedure, and likely management impact

source_original.rationale: Preoperative laboratory testing (individualized based on the client's health status, planned procedure, and risk factors, rather than a blanket approach for all clients) is intended to identify any underlying conditions or abnormalities (such as anemia, electrolyte imbalances, or coagulation issues) that could affect surgical or anesthesia risk, allowing the care team to optimize the client's condition or take appropriate precautions before proceeding.
source_original.source_detail: Preoperative testing is selected according to patient condition, procedure, and clinical indication rather than a universal panel; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced the nonspecific ASA homepage with current NICE NG45 recommendations that explicitly stratify testing by surgery/ASA/comorbidity and discourage routine low-value testing; removed family-member cueing and reduced difficulty to easy.

audit_findings.currentness: NG45 remains published as current NICE guidance as checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final D matches explicit stratified recommendations and clinical-indication logic.

distractor_audit.C: Tests supplement rather than replace clinical assessment.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: D uniquely captures the individualized testing principle.
audit_findings.blueprint: Preoperative diagnostic testing fits Reduction of Risk Potential.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked NG45 Overview and Recommendations tables; D remains unique.
